contentBlocks.text: This week you built real sentences. Today let's put three of them together into your very first short story, written in Gurmukhi script.

Read this short story, one sentence at a time: ਮੈਂ ਘਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ। ਮੈਂ ਪਾਣੀ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ। ਮੈਂ ਖੇਡਦਾ ਹਾਂ। (Main ghar jaanda haan. Main paani peenda haan. Main khedda haan. — I go home. I drink water. I play.) Notice every word in this story is one you already know! Practice reading it a few times, getting a little faster and more confident each time.
You just read your very first Punjabi story, entirely in Gurmukhi script! Tomorrow is review day, where we'll bring together everything from this whole week.

objectives: Read a three-sentence story in Gurmukhi script, built entirely from this week's known vocabulary
Retell the story's meaning in their own words
materialsNeeded: Printed 'Reading Our First Short Story' worksheet
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Read the three-sentence story together slowly, one sentence at a time.
2. Ask the child to explain what each sentence means.
3. Practice reading the whole story again, a bit faster and more confidently.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace the story and practice reading it once more.
5. Close by having the child 'read' the story aloud to a family member.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one sentence at a time, reading it multiple times before moving to the next
Ready for more: ask the child to write their own fourth sentence to add to the story, using this week's vocabulary
For a child who enjoys performing, have them act out each sentence while reading it aloud
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a reading-fluency activity — check that the child can read all three sentences and explain their meaning, at whatever pace feels comfortable.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Reading a short story built entirely from known vocabulary is the Grade 2 Punjabi course's stated goal (the course's stated 'reading short stories' focus), showing that this week's sentence-building skills translate into real reading.
